title: Calendar Flow Pressure
market_niche: Regular month-end windows in liquid ETFs where scheduled rebalancing, contribution flows, and reporting behavior may create short-lived return pressure.
phenomenon: Returns may differ around predeclared calendar windows because some participants trade for calendar, rebalance, allocation, or reporting reasons rather than fresh expected-return information.
counterparty_or_forced_actor: Asset allocators, retirement flows, target-date funds, model portfolios, fund managers, and benchmark-aware allocators with month-end or quarter-end process constraints.
why_edge_might_exist: Calendar-driven flow can create predictable temporary pressure when capital is allocated or repositioned on a schedule.
why_large_funds_might_ignore_it: The effect may be small, crowded, timing-sensitive, and hard to scale after spreads, market impact, and operational constraints.

institutional_constraint_evidence.expected_daily_dollar_volume: high for broad ETFs but lower for sector and niche ETFs
institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_strategy_capacity: unknown until turnover, spread, and market-impact assumptions are measured
institutional_constraint_evidence.number_of_opportunities_per_year: roughly eight regular month-end windows per year after excluding quarter-end month-ends

expected_capacity: Likely moderate in SPY and lower in less-liquid ETFs; edge should be assumed small and fragile until tested with costs.
execution_constraints: no date-window tuning after seeing returns
persistence_mechanism: Month-end allocation, reporting, and rebalance processes may recur because they are tied to investor and institutional operating calendars.
crowding_risk: High in broad ETFs because calendar effects are widely known and easy to monitor.
edge_decay_trigger: The thesis should weaken if the effect concentrates in one era, fails after realistic costs, or depends on shifting the entry/exit window after seeing results.
observable_prediction: Regular month-end windows excluding quarter-end overlap should show stronger drawdown-adjusted behavior than non-event exposure for at least some liquid ETFs.
falsification_tests: Reject if the prespecified strategy fails costs, train/test, or date sensitivity.
Reject if performance depends on broad timing sweeps after seeing results.
Weaken if event-day, pre-event, and post-event behavior disagree across eras without a clear mechanism.
Weaken if results are attractive only versus cash but poor versus buy-and-hold for the stated objective.
suggested_validation: Run one prespecified regular-month-end timing strategy before any timing sweep.
Compare against buy-and-hold and cash separately.
Treat a valid negative result as evidence against the exact trade timing, not a repo failure.
references: Prior tracked no-trade event study in docs/experiments/calendar-rebalance-event-study.md
